execution_separate: cpu-output.json另存真正執行的數字；本檔記透明推導，不冒稱手算是執行。

softmax.substitution: z=[2,1,0]; divide numerator/denominator by exp(2), so p=[1,exp(-1),exp(-2)]/(1+exp(-1)+exp(-2))
softmax.single_answer_ce: L=-ln(p_2)=ln(exp(2)+exp(1)+1)=2.407605964...; dL/dp=-1/p<0 for 0<p<=1, so smaller true-class probability gives larger loss.

nll.formula: For fixed valid targets V with conditional probabilities p_t, L_total=-ln(product_{t in V}p_t)=sum_{t in V}[-ln(p_t)]; mean=L_total/|V| for |V|>0.
nll.conditions: Condition on the supplied correct prefix; no independence assumption is needed for sequential chain-rule factors. Arbitrary loss masks define a conditional scoring objective, not automatically an unconditional full-text likelihood. No class weights or label smoothing here. Empty V needs a separate convention.

bigram.formula: For c_ij>=0 and C_i=sum_j c_ij>0, q_ij=c_ij/C_i>=0 and sum_j q_ij=1.
bigram.conditions: A zero-count row cannot be normalized. Linked 1.5 adds one to every cell, which makes C_i positive; glossary is read in this explicit course context.

temperature.formula: For finite logits z and T>0, q_i(T)=exp(z_i/T)/Z(T). q_i/q_j=exp((z_i-z_j)/T), hence pairwise order/argmax is unchanged. H(T)=ln Z(T)-E_q[z]/T, and dH/dT=Var_q(z)/T^3>=0.
temperature.conditions: Changing T changes sharpness at fixed logits, not parameters. T=0 is undefined; all-equal logits remain uniform. This does not ensure calibration, correctness, fixed response length, reasoning effort, or preserved confidence ordering across different questions.

gradient.formula: For differentiable scalar L(theta), component i of grad is partial L/partial theta_i with all other coordinates fixed; plain gradient descent is theta_new=theta_old-lr*grad. Along a scalar chain sensitivities multiply; at a fork, sum the contributions of every path.
gradient.conditions: Backprop computes gradients but does not itself update weights. General loss reduction is not guaranteed for arbitrary finite lr or nondifferentiable points. Linked 1.10 explicitly covers branch summation and 1.12 gives an excessive-lr counterexample.

adam.conditions: With m0=v0=0, beta1=.9,beta2=.999 and g=[1,100], first step approximately [lr,lr] for tiny eps; later histories can differ. m is first moment, v second raw moment, not centered variance or a quality guarantee.

lora.formula: W is d_out by d_in, A is r by d_in, B is d_out by r; h=Wx+(alpha/r)BAx; rank(BA)<=min(rank(A),rank(B))<=r.
lora.conditions: LoRA r names the configured bottleneck dimension/rank upper bound. At zero B, actual rank(BA)=0 even when configured r>0. A/B and settings depend on the matching base and insertion locations; no inference-speed or memory-quality ratio follows.

resume.formula: A deterministic next update is U(theta,m,v,t,lr,batch,random_draws,implementation). Equal weights alone do not determine it; history, schedule/data progress and applicable RNG states must also match.
resume.conditions: Necessary states are not by themselves a universal guarantee of bitwise reproducibility across software versions, devices, or nondeterministic kernels; linked 5.7 states this limit.
